newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Confident Australian stocks open at fresh highs.
newsitem.headline: Confident Australian stocks open at fresh highs.

text.p: A confident Australian share market hit fresh highs at the open on Wednesday after U.S. markets went ahead yet again.

Reserve Bank of Australia inaction on interest rates after its Tuesday meeting failed to dent local enthusiasm and the benchmark All Ordinaries index jumped 14.5 points to 2,735.7, surpassing the previous record high of 2,728.5 reached on June 30.
"We seem to have followed the Dow and gone in for a bit of a buying spree," said Jim Tredenick, senior dealer at Brisbane brokerage, Nevitts Ltd, noting the breadth of the rally.
"There is obviously good buying in the banks with most of them up strongly today but basically it is across the board."

Sector leader National Australia Bank hit a record high A$19.20 (A$14.40) before easing back, while the best of the rest was Commonwealth Bank which added one percent to touch the A$16.00 level early.
Among the key miners, Rio Tinto leapt 1.8 percent to A$22.88 folllowing a strong performance in London trade.

Shares in transport and healthcare group Mayne Nickless shot up, jumping nearly four percent to A$8.00 after news that Cable & Wireless Plc had doubled its stake in Optus Communications Pty ltd to 49 percent.

Mayne, which owns 24.9 percent of Optus, the second largest local telecommunications carrier, welcomed the deal, saying it reduced its underwriting exposure to the rollout of local telephony services.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of greater than two to one, while about 40 percent of stocks traded remained unchanged.
